# dsh-pulse-rail
English | 中文
Turn the DeepSeek Harness **turn-navigation rail** into a music visualiser: every thin bar grows and
thickens with the system audio that is playing right now.
|  | A ♪ button sits right above the bottom-left user row. It opens a slider panel; every change is
written back to `config.json` immediately — no restart. |

- **Windows, no admin, no drivers, no third-party runtime.** System audio is captured with WASAPI
*s

hared-mode loopback* by a tiny self-contained helper (`lib/pulse-tap.exe`, built from
`lib/pulse-tap

.cs` with the in-box .NET Framework compiler).
- **Nothing but the bars change.** Bar length tracks

its frequency band; bar thickness follows the
beat. No glow, no colour, no shadow — pure geometry, a

nd the whole thing is a compositor-only
`transform: scale()`, so the right edge never jitters.
- **N

ative behaviour is untouched.** Hover previews, click-to-jump and wheel scrolling of the rail
keep w
orking exactly as before; with silence the bars return pixel-for-pixel to the stock look.

y default render device (headphones, USB DAC, HDMI, …) |

2. Enable it, then **restart DSH** (the host half is composed at boot).

## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

* **Host half** (`lib/index.js` + `lib/tap.js`): lazily spawns the capture helper, keeps the last
fr

ame, serves it on same-origin routes. The helper is killed after 20 s without a request, is
restarte

d with back-off if it dies, and self-terminates if the host stops heart-beating it.
* **Browser half

** (`lib/client.js`): locates the rail by geometry (narrow column of small marks
near the right edge

, with a `button[data-index]` fallback), re-maps every frame to the *currently
rendered* mark count,

and writes one custom property per mark. Length and thickness are both
expressed as `transform: sca

le()` on the mark's `::before`, with `transform-origin: 100% 50%`.
Because the scroll container of t

he rail clips horizontally at 28 px, the plugin widens that
container leftwards (right edge unchange

d, hit area unchanged, `pointer-events` passed through)
so long bars are actually visible.
* **Silen
ce** removes every override — the rail is byte-for-byte the app's own rendering again.
## Privacy
The helper reads the system mix **in memory** and emits only band levels (12 floats) plus RMS/peak.

No audio is recorded, buffered or written to disk. It runs only while the page asks for data and
sto

ps on its own 20 s after the last request; you can also watch it as `pulse-tap.exe` in Task
Manager,
or set `"enabled": false`.

iscovery reports |

p) |

es (e.g. `[dsh-pulse-rail] …`) |
| `lib\pulse-tap.exe --fps 30` | run the helper by hand and watch t

he JSON stream |
| Conversation squeezed to a thin strip / UI looks shifted left on long sessions |
0.4.0 regression — **upgrade to 0.4.1**; reloading the window recovers temporarily (regression test:
`node tools/rail-target-test.mjs`) |

No sound in the bars? Play something and check `/pulse-rail/state` → `playing`. If `running` is
fals

e, look at `lastError` (a USB/Bluetooth endpoint that reports all-zero samples is re-initialised
aut
omatically after 5 s of silence).
